audit_findings.title: The convertible-note denominator describes a different claim from the OE numerator
audit_findings.magnitude: 3.944270 million shares, 11.9% of the 33.190463 million denominator; removing only this block raises computed base value from $103.59 to approximately $117.55 per share before scenario-consistent incremental dilution
audit_findings.evidence: Upon conversion, the Company will pay cash up to the aggregate principal amount of the 2030 Convertible Notes to be converted and pay or deliver, as the case may be, cash, shares of the Company's common stock, or a combination of cash and shares of the Company's common stock, at the Company's election, in respect of the remainder, if any, of the Company's conversion obligation in excess of the aggregate principal amount of the 2030 Convertible Notes being converted.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated denominator error. Principal must be settled in cash, while the valuation counts every underlying share despite retaining note interest in OE. Only the excess conversion value can create shares, and the note hedge may offset that dilution. The resulting approximately $13.96 per-share base-case difference is large enough to change the conclusion relative to the $102.60 market price.
audit_findings.action: Rerun each scenario using incremental shares attributable only to conversion value above the adjusted conversion price, then apply the permitted settlement election and 2030 note hedge consistently with interest-bearing equity-level OE.

audit_findings.title: The warrant ceiling ignores strike prices and exercise proceeds
audit_findings.magnitude: 4.5 million shares, 13.6% of the 33.190463 million denominator; removing only this block raises computed base value from $103.59 to approximately $119.83 per share
audit_findings.evidence: For the period from issuance through December 31, 2025, the average share price was below the Warrant strike price of $ 182.94 per share, and therefore 3.9 million shares were considered antidilutive.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated denominator error. The 3.9 million 2030 warrants have a $182.94 strike, while the 0.6 million 2026 warrants had a $245.41 adjusted strike and were expected to expire unexercised in August 2026. All supplied scenario values are below those strikes, so full-cover inclusion at zero exercise cost materially understates the common-equity claim. The approximately $16.24 base-case difference can change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Remove the expired 2026 warrants and rerun each scenario using treasury-stock incremental dilution for the 2030 warrants, including exercise proceeds and any applicable anti-dilution adjustments.

audit_findings.title: Serial-acquirer amortization may represent a real replacement cost
audit_findings.magnitude: $54.176 million of filed 2025 intangible amortization, including $38.7 million in the OEM Segment; 23.6% of the $229.3 million anchor, but the economic replacement portion is unquantified
audit_findings.evidence: Amortization expense on intangible assets for the OEM Segment was $38.7 million in 2025, compared to $39.8 million in 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved possibility, not a demonstrated error. The filed amortization is large enough to matter, and LCII spent $112.7 million on acquisitions in 2025, but the record does not show whether amortization was added back in the OE worksheet or whether acquisition-related reinvestment was included in the RONTA growth charge. Accounting amortization also does not by itself establish the recurring economic replacement cost.
audit_findings.action: Trace all intangible-amortization adjustments in the OE worksheet and reconstruct acquisition spending, including consideration and goodwill premiums, needed to sustain the assumed growth; rerun OE and growth using the supported recurring replacement amount.

audit_findings.title: The anchor may retain a nonrecurring property-sale gain
audit_findings.magnitude: $19.716 million property gain and $8.859 million debt-extinguishment loss; at the filed 26.2% tax rate, approximately $14.55 million and $6.54 million after tax, respectively, for a net $8.01 million or 3.5% of anchor if both remain
audit_findings.evidence: The sales resulted in a total net gain on the sale of real estate of $19.7 million for the year ended December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The normalization error is unresolved because the worksheet trace is absent, but its potential materiality is established. If neither item was normalized, the net after-tax anchor overstatement would reduce computed base value by approximately $3.39 per share, from $103.59 to about $100.20, reversing the conclusion relative to the $102.60 price. Direction is mixed because retaining the gain overstates value, while failing to add back the loss understates value; asymmetric treatment can therefore distort either way.
audit_findings.action: Trace both items from net income and cash-flow reconciliation into the $229.3 million anchor, normalize both symmetrically after tax, and rerun all scenarios if either remains in recurring OE.

audit_findings.title: Residual Dutch pension funding may be an unbridged senior claim
audit_findings.evidence: The Company has purchased annuity contracts from an insurance company to cover the vested benefits of the defined pension plans; however, future indexation and cost of living adjustments for all participants remains applicable, and the Company remains liable for future funding.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved existing-claim issue rather than merely a forward-looking risk. Annuities cover vested benefits, but LCII remains liable for future indexation and cost-of-living funding. The filings do not quantify the residual actuarial obligation, expected contributions, or the amount already recorded, so the record cannot establish materiality or a bridge adjustment.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the latest actuarial report and funded-status reconciliation, identify recorded pension assets or liabilities and expected indexation contributions, then deduct any unrecorded senior claim in the bridge or reflect recurring contributions in normalized OE without double counting.
